floor_history.headline: Gap is 100% frame-layout, not codegen: 139/139 insns identical, only the 9 reload spill slots sit at sp+4 mod 8 vs target's +0 — traced to cc1's big-endian bigend_correction on 8-rounded spill slots;
Structural axis measured dead across 11 variants; session 1's func_8006BD28 existence proof was authorized canonical asm, and a tree-wide census plus a cc1psx counter-exhibit show the +4 spill offset

frontier.hypothesis: The remaining 0-mod-8 route the source proof leaves open is the slot-reuse branch at reload1.c:2384 — a spill slot allocated in a wider mode and then reused by an SImode pseudo inherits the wider slot's base with NO big-endian correction. If any real BB2 translation unit ever takes that path, the construct that triggers it is the only known C-level lever on the congruence.
frontier.mechanism: alter_reg's reuse branch (x = spill_stack_slot[from_reg]) skips the bigend_correction entirely and only rebuilds the MEM in the pseudo's own mode at adjust 0. It requires from_reg != -1 (the pseudo was hard-allocated and then spilled by spill_hard_reg, not left unallocated by global alloc) and a prior wider-mode spill from that same hard register.
frontier.next_probe: Forensics modality: use the instrumented cc1 at tools/gcc-2.7.2/cc1 (NOT build/cc1 — see [[instrumented-cc1-location]]) to log every alter_reg call with (pseudo, from_reg, mode, total_size, chosen path, final offset) while compiling the real src/*.c translation units, and count how often the 2384 reuse path is taken and with what modes. If it never fires anywhere in BB2, the congruence has no C lever at all and the class is closed; if it fires, the triggering construct is named. Do NOT recompile src/text1b.c whole for this — instrument on smaller TUs first.

frontier.hypothesis: func_80060E38 is not an isolated hard function but a member of a 29-function class defined by 'target contains a stride-8 reload-spill block', all of which are blocked by the same measured fork property, and the class should be dispositioned as a class rather than ground one function at a time.
frontier.mechanism: Census: 29 stride-8 spill blocks tree-wide, all at 0 mod 8, all rule-carrying, none ever matched; the offset is === -GET_MODE_SIZE(mode) (mod 8) under our BYTES_BIG_ENDIAN cc1, and cc1psx fed identical input produces target's congruence. Every surface that could change it (the cc1 binary/configuration, the Makefile, prologue_config.json, regfix/asmfix) is outside the grind edit surface, and [[no-compiler-divergence]] forbids the compiler-side fix.
frontier.next_probe: This is an owner-surface question, not a grind-surface one, and the driver has NOT declared exhaustion for this function — so it must not be escalated yet. Whichever session is eventually assigned escalation modality should file the class (not just func_80060E38) in docs/grind/decisions.md, citing spillscan2.txt, the closed-form proof, and the cc1psx counter-exhibit — and must NOT cite Ruling-2, whose scope limit explicitly excludes non-crashing fork divergences.

frontier.hypothesis: A rederived C shape whose 139 instructions match target but whose 9 stack slots are NOT align == -1 reload spills would sidestep the correction entirely.
frontier.mechanism: The +4 is exclusive to the align == -1 path (8-byte rounding => bigend_correction 4). Slots created by any other route (align == 0 declared locals, assign_stack_temp) carry no correction.
frontier.next_probe: Partly measured already and looking dead: v_locals.c showed declared locals get stride 4, and target's stride 8 for 4-byte values implies align == -1 implies +4. The only untried sub-case is assign_stack_temp-created slots (compiler temporaries for structure/aggregate copies), which a rederive-modality session could probe by expressing the 32 constants as an aggregate initialisation or a memcpy-shaped construct and reading the emitted slot stride. Expect it to change the instruction count away from 139 — measure with sandbox --disable all before believing anything.
